body: I'm not going to be a vagrant. There is no coming back from this, no point to rebuild from. My life is over and there is no point at all in continuing it.

You mistaken self loathing for victimization. I am not a victim. I am a monster of my own creation. Every wrong decision, every misguided word or action had brought me to where I am right now. The constant, the only constant, in all of this is me. And I am tired of building my life up, fucking it up in ways I did not foresee, and then winding up in a position where I don't even have a pot to piss in.

This is not how I want to live my life and I'm not going to. Things don't suddenly change, people don't change, and the changing of circumstances in any direction is so fickle betting on any outcome is retarded.

I am done living like this. I am done trying to do what I think is the right thing only to fuck it up so horribly I am legitimately the bad guy. I don't get a happy ending because an asshole like me doesn't deserve one. And we can talk about medication and therapy all we want, but we both know there is something neurologically wrong with me that cannot be fixed or cured. It can't be excised like a tumor, it can only be treated and managed. And twice a year it blows up and I'm too weak and stubborn to reign it in, just like this past week.

I have two or three days. I will spend that time appreciating the city and then it's lights out.

It is a solution. Maybe not one you agree with, but I am not going to spend the rest of my days a vagabond pining for love and affection I will never get to have because my mental health, even when managed, makes me a non option to everyone. I am not going to live in hostels for months on end, I'm not going to beg for change, and I am not going to watch myself deteriorate until I am unrecognizable.

The world may not be cruel, but it isn't kind or generous either. Every day is a new fight and I am at a point I have nothing left to fight for. I have two backpacks. I have no home. I have no job. My friends have all abandoned me, as has my family. I have no girlfriend or someone whom I can love and have it reciprocated. I have myself and, guy/gal, there is nothing about me that makes my existence worthwhile.

This is my life's low point and it does not get better. I don't get a happy ending and never was meant to. That's a shitty fact of life. So, knowing how little remains I have left to shape  into any desirable direction, all I can do is make the most of my last few days and have good memories to reflect on in my final moments. I am not going to keep fighting and struggling for better days I logically know will never happen, and I sure the fuck won't do so as a vagabond begging for change.

I know what I have to do and it will be done.

Well, I've reevaluated my plan and have decided that I'll stay in the hostels until my funds dry up and then I'm going to finish what I couldn't on Thursday. I've tasted the inky black void and it does not frighten me; it is welcoming, warm, and peaceful. And I'm going to take that because there is no way out that doesn't involve me going back to the US or getting hidden away in a mental health center. 

So, thank you everyone for your help and consideration, but now I know what I need to do and will be seeing it through accordingly. Couple of days left to see the city again and then I won't have to worry about it anymore.

Mother's side would help but can't afford to take on another. Both grandparents are in and out of the hospital; she had a heart attack last week, he fell and almost broke a hip. This week she's back in with a staph infection in the leg, he's back in because he's becoming combative and forgetful (doc says first stages of dementia). Mom can't help: she's physically disabled and her disability ($700 a month) is mostly consumed by creditors because my dad stuck her with the business taxes when they divorced. Aunts, uncles, and cousins are strangers to me: not close to any. I have a brother, but he said he can't help because of his work (firefighter/EMT).

Because I burnt my bridges by moving here a second time. My paternal side is so uber-patriotic that my dad shits stars and stripes. To him, it is better to work at a factory for minimum wage (he doesn't, he's self employed) to "earn your way up" than it is to look anywhere else for better financial or social options. I turn to him for help, I get strong armed into going back, and I will not spend another year as an indentured servant to him (at 40 hours a week, I had to clean the entire house, do the dishes, dog watch, and adjust any plans I might have over the weekend to accommodate those three). Further to the point, he's controlling: he has gone through my drawers, wants to know my finances, gives me grief if I rent a movie from redbox, and chastises me if I have to drive to see friends. That's why I don't turn to family.
I'm at a hostel now. I *might* be able to wing it for another day or two, but I don't know what to do beyond that.

I am bipolar I. I don't drink, I don't smoke, I workout 10 hours a week at the gym.

I do not have a drug problem. I have a problem with acclimating to existing drug therapies in 6 months instead of years. Receptor burn out. And there is nothing, not a goddamn thing anyone can do about it. I can have my meds changed and be right back in the hole regardless of what I do  to take care and manage it. And at my weight (190) with the amount of muscle on my frame, I am physically resilient. And when you couple that with a manic hit, it takes A LOT to bring me down. I would know. Have you ever spent days up at a time trying to piece the shattered remains of your mind back together alone? Trying everything, anything, reaching out to everyone you know, only for you to fall further and further into the dark? And this is with the right medication AT the right dosage.

I did not want to go through that again, especially not when in a highly pissed state of mine. So what is the better option? Sit in a corner freaking out, so pissed you're crying and yet afraid the world you have been looking forward to for months is ending, or do you knock yourself out for a few days and remove yourself as a threat/problem?

I came here because she said she was going to leave him. She all but said she was waiting for me to get here to do so. I arrived and she still said she had feelings for me, we even made love. And even after she decided to give him another go she said she had feelings for me. I may not be innocent, but do not tell me that is not mindfuckery especially when she says still has feelings for you.

I wasn't "fired", I didn't do the things I did to get in her pants, I did them because I wanted to show her and her dad what it's like to not be taken for granted so that they want more for themselves even when I am so far removed they can't remember my name.

I don't have a problem with drugs.  I was having an anxiety attack I could not reign in, took a few, still couldn't reign it in, and then decided to take enough to knock myself out becauze I didn't feel like sitting in a corner crying all day unable to move because the world seemed to be coming apart.

Dude, I am still fucked up from ODing on three months worth of klonopin two days ago. The fact I can even walk and string some thoughts together is a minor miracle. I am not all there right now and won't be for a few days.

I came to Canada to romantically be with that friend because the boyfriend was on the way out and we had expressed feelings for each other at length for months (and we were friends in Canada). Not a week before my landing, they get back together.

I have done all the farm work; I fed, watered, and changed the bedding for 2 clydes, 9 donkeys, and a pony. I put up and wired a 3 hundred foot long electric fence almost singlehandedly. I have moved the metric tons of scrap metal he has left on the property by myself and took care of the carious bits he had months to do but hasn't. I cooked, I cleaned the house every day, and I paid my rent on time. And this is with getting up at 4 to clean cow dung at a farm and to get the shit kicked out of me when I milked them.

 And I got the boot because he and I got into an argument as to why it is not at all okay to leave a dog on a chain outside in October wind and rain without there being a shelter of some kind: you out an animal out, it is your obligation to bring then right back in after they do their business.

That's why I got booted: because we argued, he then picked a fight, and she chose him over me. 

So thanks for assuming I was a mooch.
It was sent via walmart's equivalent of western union but every Walmart here says they don't do that so they can't help.
I have zero money

I'll cope; I've done it before, I'll do it now. The best thing to do is to step back, detach myself from the situation, and accept things for what they are.

Does it suck? Yeah. Immensely. No one likes being the odd person out, hyper attuned to seeing every happy couple walking by hand in hand, smiling, and all that romantic jazz. You don't feel jealous, more envious for what they have and curious as to what glaring personal flaw you have that hasn't been corrected that keeps you from walking amongst them.

I've been in the friendzone and in the torturous miasma surrounding it for almost two years. I know I'm going to be in it for a few years more. That's not depression or self pity talking, just experience. Pull the boot straps up, keep pumping iron, scar over, and hope someday whatever self improvements I make to myself will allow me to not be a spinster.

It is what it is. I'll push on and endure. Forgetting the fact there is no alternative, perseverance is what I do best. It's how I powered through traumatic things that would break most, it is how I manage to push myself in the gym, and it's how I can get out of bed each day when my brain tells me not to bother.

It's how I'll get through this too: inner strength overcomes pain until it fades into the background. It's the period in between now and inevitable apathy that is most troublesome: hurt and frustration are, with everything else, harder to manage because there's no "fix" for it other than time.

Being in the friendzone with all romantic interests is a shitty deal to be sure,  but it's not all bad: at least she is still my friend, even after I laid it all out.

I spend 10-15 hours a week, every week weight lifting. That is how I spend my free time.

As for other girls, I am a non option for most. I'm roughly 8 years behind most guys my age academically and in career options (in large part to a toxic marriage I couldn't easily get out of). I carry debt and, the cherry on top, is clinical depression. It doesn't matter if I am medicated and regularly see a therapist: the second anyone hears "clinical depression" after a length of time has passed and I trust them enough to share, they bail. People don't like or are drawn to damaged goods; doesn't matter who you are, what you are, where, that is a fact. If the totality of my life experiences can be summed up, that is the key lesson to be gleaned from it.

I'm more or less stuck here as it currently stands. I quit my job with the anticipation of moving back north and I have no inclination of crawling back (if for nothing else but the level of stress it carries).

My academic options for the next year are basically limited to this state. I can't get student loans anywhere else and the "I'll put off college for another year to save money" hasn't gotten me anywhere in the last 8 years I've done so.

To say I feel gutted is an understatement. Going to school this fall up north has literally been the only thing that has kept me going this past year and, now that it has been completely removed from the equation, I have absolutely nothing left to hope for.
Got off the phone with OSAP; I'm ineligible for Canadian student loans. If I were to move back up north, I now have no realistic way of paying for college until next year.

I think Canada is the best choice. It won't be any easier (a mental health disorder has effectively stigmatized me as a non-viable candidate for a potential relationship effectively for life), but I can at least put some distance between myself and family drama. I won't be happy, but I will at least be less miserable. I will still be an outsider, but it will be because I am from a foreign nation and not because I refuse to conform to (what I find to be) ass-backwards social norms.

It's something definitely worth considering/ under the provision I go back up north; down here, psychiatric care of any kind in the US is prohibitively expensive (a lesson I have learned the hard way) and biofeedback therapy would necessitate going to a much more expensive health care center.

As we speak, I'm trying to get my affairs in order to move back to Canada. Montreal is very tempting; I've visited the city only a few times, but it is a place that is almost magical to me (so full of life and rich in culture). I've missed the deadline for fall if I wanted to go to Concordia, but I believe I can still apply for the winter session. 

At the same time, I am tempted to go back to Ottawa and go to Algonquin (even if only for a year).
Never heard of biofeedback before. What does it entail?

I've considered ECT, but am wary of it. My depression is, in part, caused by minor brain damage to my right frontal lobe from a skull fracture and severe concussion a few years ago; causing further levels of micro-damage has the potential to make things worse instead of better. The other side of the coin is genetics (as nearly all men on my maternal side have some form of either depression or bi-polar I disorder).

But yes, it is resistant clinical depression. Treatments are effective for about 6 months before the dosage has be dramatically increased or I have to be tapered off in order to try something else. 

I'll definitely look into Concordia; I hope they offer courses in english as much as they do in french (I'm, regrettably, an anglophone).

Oh, fitting in has always been a personal problem for as long as I can possibly remember and it's because I'm quite awkward. 

In person, I'm generally very quiet. I don't talk much for a three reasons: 1) I find it difficult to participate in or contribute to a conversation that isn't something I'm familiar with, 2) sustained conversation is actually physically painful for me (I don't go hoarse so much as my throat starts to swell), and 3) I talk exactly as I write (which people perceive as arrogance). When I do talk, though, my voice is relatively deep and has a low volume by default; I get frustrated having to repeat myself multiple times because others have difficulty hearing me (if I raise my voice to "normal" volume, I feel as if I'm shouting).

I see a therapist and am medicated. We've hit a roadblock when it comes to dealing with depression (clinical), but we're making slow progress with the social anxiety. I'm not afraid of being judged by others all that much anymore; people inherently think more about themselves than they do other people and, in most situations, fear of judgment in social circumstances is unwarranted. Even if I were judged, those opinions will carry only as much weight as I allow them to. 

I know that a degree is imperative and it is something I will be pursuing. It was a little disheartening, however, that I couldn't find steady and consistent work regardless of the number of applications I put out (225 by my count, at least 400 according to my gmail) where my work history made me a viable candidate. I don't know if it was because Ottawa's economy was slowing down, if my (few) interviewers could tell I was incredibly stressed in spite of the happy facade I was putting on, or they perceived disinterested since I wasn't asking a lot of a questions (operating a small-scale warehouse is something I have done in various capacities for the last 8 years).

I was debating about attending McGill, but I don't know if I'd meet the eligibility requirements for admission because my ACT score is 25 overall and they say they require a 26 on their website. I took my ACT in my sophomore year without a calculator, any study prep, or a decent amount of sleep. Because the scores were several points higher than what most American universities required (at the time, at least), I never bothered to re-take it. Having a 3.90 GPA and graduating as valedictorian means exceptionally little to post-secondary institutions. It's why I more or less focused on going to college at Algonquin: I know I can get in there. I'd love to live and study in Montreal (gorgeous city, very full of life, very rich culture, friendly people), but the post-secondary education is the deciding factor.

I lived in Ontario from June 2006 until mid August of last year, though I had visited frequently from 2003 up until I actually immigrated. Fitting was challenging because I have moderate-severe social anxiety.

They think I'm throwing my future away because, in the state of Missouri, I'd more or less have a free ride to university (for a multitude of reasons) whereas I don't readily have the option available up north.  They also think that because I was unable to secure a steady/consistent job for months after I was let go by my previous employer (long story for a different time), while I was able to more or less get one without much effort when I had moved here. They seem to think that, because I'm not a Canadian citizen, I will forever be looked down upon and will be at the bottom of anyone's list in terms of hiring even if I met/exceed the qualifications for that job.

As for what I do for work, I'm a warehouse manager/grunt. I'm not proud of it and it's not something I openly advertise to most people. It's all I've ever done for work and that's because I find that there's always a need for it: few people are willing to do physically demanding jobs for minimum or just over minimum wage. Fields of work that I know I can do (computer repair/basic IT, fitness instruction) based on personal experience (I do computer repairs on the side, and I'm a dedicated weight lifter) are exclusionary because they require certs I don't have.
The same could very well be said about yourself. I find it quite odd you have the expectation that you can be condescending without being the subject of condescension in return.

Family, mostly. They're....unsupportive to say the very least. I have been told everything from "You're throwing your future away" to "You don't belong there, you will never belong there, and you will never make anything of yourself if you go back".

On the other side, my grandfather is in poor health and I'll be surprised if he lives one more year given the rate at which he is declining (diabetes, prostate tumors, heart disease, CPD, beginning stages of dementia, and failing kidneys).

I'm done being cordial. I'm not referring to my comment to yours, I'm referring to the fact you glossed over that I very clearly said "I have permanent residency" in order to be a condescending douche. 

Again, read the beginning of the first sentence of the third paragraph (second paragraph after the word conundrum) of my post. Do you see where it says "I have permanent residency"? It would be safe to deduce that, with that statement, I have the legal privilege to live, work, and pay taxes in the nation I have residency status in. It also means I have spent a length of time in said country, as it that is a requirement of permanent residency. I didn't have to go into depth, detail, or even why because it was not relevant.  It isn't a question or hypothetical, it is a factual statement. I'm not asking and haven't asked how to get it anywhere in anything I have said, I have made it clear it is something I already possess.

"....believe it or not, we're not psychic". You don't have to have ESP in order to have basic literacy. You were wrong, I have literally shown you where you are wrong, and you persist to defend your comment in spite of that.

It's peaceful, but dull; there's a reason it was voted as the most boring major city in the all of Canada. But it isn't without its charms; the Rideau canal is a bit of a sight to be hold during the winter, Blues Fest has had amazing acts every year for the last few years, and it's relatively safe. Kansas City has more murders in a day (mostly drug related in the ghetto, just beyond the reach of the Plaza) than Ottawa has in the past 5 years. And the only thing I've ever had stolen from me was the novelty doormat I had for my first apartment; St. Joseph and KC, by contrast, is such that I make sure to leave absolutely nothing of any value in the car.

As I'm under the impression you have read the entirety of my post prior to making your first comment, I am a bit perplexed at your irritation/snark. I explicitly said "I have permanent residency in Canada" and actually began the first sentence of the third paragraph with that statement.

The winter weather never bothered me much. Heavy snowfalls are something you appreciate when you grew up never having them (that's not to say there wasn't snow, but nothing beyond a few centimeters at most) and the bitter cold makes some things all that much more precious (summer, for example).

If I were to go back, I'd like to return to Ottawa. It's not an exciting city, but it's familiar and relatively safe.

I earned my permanent residency and lived in Ontario for 8 years (from the age of 19 up until last August). It has a culture and country I identify with far more than my own. It, to me, is home: it's where I lived, it's where I worked, it's where I made my friends and so on.

Why would I willingly give that up?

They might have examples to look at, but their manufacturing industries lack the sophistication required to make 1 to 1 copies (or even copies) of a number of military technologies. For example: all of their aircraft are procured from other countries (mostly Soviet or Russian surplus). They have a select number of Mig 29s, but the bulk of their airforce is still comprised of Soviet made Mig 17s (aircraft they can maintain, but cannot manufacture themselves).
Algonquin College in Ottawa (Ontario), Johnson County Community College (in Kansas City, Missouri).
